name: Maple-Teriyaki Salmon Sushi Bowl with Cucumber & Edamame (Prep-Ahead)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe utilizes 4 medium food storage containers.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 cup jasmine rice
2 cups chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.primary_message: Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place maple syrup, soy sauce, oil, vinegar, and garlic powder in a medium bowl, then whisk to combine the marinade.
instructions.secondary_message:
pure maple syrup
2 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
1 tbsp rice vinegar
½ tsp garlic powder

instructions.primary_message: If using salmon with skin, place the fillet, skin-side down, on a cutting board. Holding the tail end (or corner) firmly, use a knife to cut between the flesh and skin; continue to cut through the length of the fillet (take care not to cut through the skin); discard the skin.
Cut the salmon into 1-inch cubes. Add to the bowl with the marinade, stir to coat, and set aside for 10 minutes.
While the salmon is marinating, wash and dry cucumber. Using a clean cutting board, cut cucumber crosswise into eights, then cut each piece lengthwise into ¼-inch thick sticks. Place on a plate.
Place edamame in the colander and rinse under hot water (from the tap) to thaw. Add to the plate with the cucumber and set aside.
When the salmon is done marinating, preheat a large skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add salmon and any leftover marinade in the bowl. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and salmon is cooked through, 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside to cool, about 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, place vinegar, maple syrup, and salt in a small bowl, then whisk to combine. Add to the pan with the cooked rice and stir to combine. Transfer rice to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer to cool, about 10 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tbsp rice vinegar
1 tsp pure maple syrup
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Divide cooled rice, teriyaki salmon, cucumber, and edamame between the food storage containers, then sprinkle with sesame seeds. Cover, refrigerate until ready to eat, and enjoy!
